report.verdict: A strong but flattered print: Gaming Win +30% to €67.1m (~$77.2m) was only +23% at constant currency, July's World Cup tail did the heavy lifting, and all of the +45% Adj. EBITDA growth to €4.2m (~$4.8m) comes from adding back a €1.4m LTIP charge — unadjusted EBITDA actually fell 9% YoY. Spain remains the profit engine (29% margin), Mexico is growing on price not volume (actives -3%, spend/active +43%) under a stepped-up gaming tax, and management explicitly guided Q4 to single-digit growth while holding FY26 guidance rather than raising it; the parent's break-up sale process is the overhang nobody on the call asked about.
summary: **Headline beat on growth, in line on profit cadence.** Q3-26 IFRS revenue €62.6m (~$72.0m), +31% YoY vs €47.7m (~$54.9m); Gaming Win €67.1m (~$77.2m), +30%; Adj. EBITDA €4.2m (~$4.8m), +45% (+€1.3m). No reliable sell-side consensus was located for this micro-cap; the result tracks ahead of the run-rate implied by the July-raised FY26 guidance (9M Gaming Win €201.0m = 76-79% of the €255-265m range after three quarters).

**Guidance reiterated, not raised — and that is the message.** FY26 outlook held at Gaming Win €255-265m (~$293-305m) and Adj. EBITDA €20-25m (~$23-29m), set on 30 Jul 2026 (raised then from €235-245m / €15-20m). CFO Arildsson pointed to the 'upper part' of the Gaming Win range; CEO Sher said they prefer to 'stay within the range and try to beat it' given Spain and FX headwinds.

**Q4 explicitly guided to single-digit Gaming Win growth.** Implied Q4-26 Gaming Win is €54-64m (~$62-74m) vs a strong Q4-25 comp of €60.7m (~$69.8m), i.e. -11% to +5%; implied Q4-26 Adj. EBITDA is €3.9-8.9m (~$4.5-10.2m) vs €6.7m (~$7.7m) in Q4-25 (derived: FY25 €13.8m less 9M-25 €7.1m). Headwinds cited: no World Cup, no peso tailwind, Spain AML/deposit-rule transition.

**Mexico drove the quarter — but on FX and price, not players.** Mexico revenue €32.9m (~$37.8m), +37%; Gaming Win €37.2m (~$42.8m), +39% reported but only +26% at constant currency (~13pp FX). Monthly actives fell 3% YoY to 85.6k while spend per active rose 43% to ~€145 (~$167). Group constant-currency Gaming Win growth was +23% vs +30% reported.

**Mexico profit went backwards despite +39% top line.** Mexico Adj. EBITDA €1.7m (~$2.0m) vs €2.0m (~$2.3m) in Q3-25; margin 5.2% of revenue (-310bps). Management blamed higher gaming taxes and marketing timing/provisions; group gaming taxes jumped 55% to €13.6m (~$15.6m), consistent with the Mexican 2026 fiscal package lifting the online gaming levy to 50% from 30% (per CasinoBeats; not independently verified in the filing).

**Spain is the profit engine and the regulatory risk.** Spain revenue/Gaming Win €24.8m (~$28.5m), +13% YoY but -10% QoQ off the World Cup-boosted Q2; Adj. EBITDA €7.2m (~$8.3m), +24%, margin 29.0% (+~260bps). Spain alone generates ~170% of group Adj. EBITDA; Mexico and Other/HQ absorb the rest.

**World Cup effect quantified only qualitatively.** Management called July 'exceptional' on the final stages of the World Cup, with acquisition slowing in August/September before stabilising with the return of the major leagues. Q2-26 (the bulk of the tournament) was the record quarter at €69.4m (~$79.8m) Gaming Win; Q3 was 3% below it sequentially. No tournament-specific Gaming Win, handle or actives figure was disclosed.

**Customer economics: quality over quantity.** Group actives 166.8k, +5% YoY but down sequentially for a second quarter (183k Q1 → 173k Q2 → 166.8k Q3); spend per active €134 (~$154), +24% YoY, flat QoQ. FTDs 91k, +7%; quarterly CPA €209 (~$240), LTM CPA stable at ~€196 (~$225). Casino 67% / sports 33% of Gaming Win.

**Marketing stepped up 37% to €25.2m (~$29.0m), 40% of revenue (vs 39%).** FY26 marketing guided to the 'high-90s', close to €100m (~$115m) including €3-4m of peso translation, vs €86m (~$99m) in FY25. FY27 is pencilled at a similar absolute level with marketing falling as a % of Gaming Win — the operating-leverage promise is pushed into 2027.

**Operating leverage is real below the marketing line.** Total opex +29% to €62.9m (~$72.3m) vs revenue +31%; platform & content +10% to €16.0m (~$18.4m, 25.6% of revenue vs 30.5%); personnel +13% to €5.2m (~$6.0m, 8.3% vs 9.6%).

**Adj. EBITDA growth is entirely LTIP add-back.** Reported EBITDA (pre-adjustments) was €2.9m (~$3.3m) vs €3.2m (~$3.7m) in Q3-25, -9%. The bridge to €4.2m Adj. EBITDA adds back a €1.4m (~$1.6m) LTIP charge (vs a €0.2m credit last year); 9M LTIP add-back is €7.6m (~$8.7m) of €16.1m Adj. EBITDA. Footnote confirms 'Other adjustments' from 2026 include shares withheld for taxes under the LTIP — i.e. part of this is cash-settled.

**Net income flattered by warrants.** Q3-26 net income €5.5m (~$6.3m) vs €1.4m includes a €3.4m (~$3.9m) non-cash fair-value gain on public warrants (CDROW) and €0.3m net interest/FX income (vs €1.4m expense). Underlying pre-tax profit ex-warrants ~€2.9m vs ~€2.4m. 9M net income €11.1m (~$12.8m) vs a €1.7m loss. EPS not disclosed in the release.

**Capital position: net cash, no debt, cash tracking EBITDA.** Total cash €65.6m (~$75.4m) at 30 Sep (of which ~€61m / ~$70m 'available for operations'), up from €62.7m at 30 Jun; Q3 cash generation €3.0m (~$3.4m), 9M €16.4m (~$18.9m), in line with 9M Adj. EBITDA €16.1m. No buyback or dividend; no leverage metric applicable.

**Metric rebrand after SEC review.** 'Net Gaming Revenue' is renamed 'Gaming Win' with historical amounts unchanged; the transcript attributes the change to an SEC review. The press release now leads with IFRS revenue, with Gaming Win expressly 'not a measure of revenue'. A governance housekeeping item, but it tells you the regulator pushed back on non-IFRS prominence.

**NFL Mexico partnership is the strategic headline.** Multi-year Official Betting Partner of the NFL in Mexico (announced 10 Sep 2026), including the NFL Mexico City Game on 22 Nov 2026 and Super Bowl LXI (Feb 2027), hospitality/VIP activations and merchandise. Q4 marketing will carry the activation cost.

**Spain regulation: AML friction now, deposit limits in 2027.** New ID and deposit requirements with nominative payment methods applied to new customers from end-October 2026 (extending to existing customers April 2027), already slowing Spanish acquisition; joint cross-operator deposit limits (default, player-adjustable) take effect March 2027. Management expects 'some slowdown', not a step-change, and will pre-brief VIPs.

**Parent break-up overhang.** Codere Group's hedge-fund owners launched a ~€2bn (~$2.3bn) whole-group sale in March 2026 (Jefferies/Macquarie) and, per Expansión (2 Nov 2026), are now weighing selling Europe, LatAm and listed Codere Online separately. Not addressed on the call; a change-of-control at the controlling shareholder is a live thesis variable.

**Other markets (Colombia, Panama, Buenos Aires) +86% on an easy comp.** Gaming Win €5.2m (~$6.0m), 8% of group; growth reflects lapping Colombia's 19% deposit tax in 2025 and strong Panama. Management flagged a possible 2027 Colombian deposit tax that could prompt reduced investment there.

**Thesis read-through.** The equity story is Spain's cash margin funding a Mexico land-grab that has so far converted +39% Gaming Win into lower EBITDA. With FX reversing, Mexican tax at 50%, Spanish AML friction and ~€100m of marketing locked in, the FY26 EBITDA range (€20-25m) looks achievable at the low-to-mid end; the 2027 margin step-up depends on marketing finally lagging Gaming Win growth.

segments.name: Spain
segments.headline: Profit engine intact — €7.2m Adj. EBITDA at a 29% margin on +13% growth — but the AML/deposit regime is already slowing acquisition and the QoQ step-down (-10%) shows how much of Q2 was World Cup.
narrative: Spain delivered revenue and Gaming Win of €24.8m (~$28.5m), up 13% year-on-year but 10% below the record €27.6m (~$31.7m) of Q2-26, which carried most of the World Cup. In Spain the two measures are identical because there is no VAT or levy wedge between what the platform records and what IFRS recognises, so the growth is clean. The drivers were balanced: average monthly actives rose 5% to 52.8k (down 3% sequentially from 54.4k), and monthly spend per active rose 7% to roughly €157 (~$180) — a far more conventional mix of volume and price than Mexico. For the nine months, revenue is €77.9m (~$89.6m), +18%, with actives +10% to 55.4k, so the quarter represents a modest deceleration against a comp that itself contained no major tournament.

Profitability was the standout. Spain Adj. EBITDA rose 24% to €7.2m (~$8.3m), a 29.0% margin, roughly 260bps better than the ~26.4% implied for Q3-25 and ahead of the 28.3% in Q2-26 despite lower revenue — which suggests marketing was pulled back after the tournament and the fixed cost base is now well covered. Put simply, Spain generated about 1.7x the group's Adj. EBITDA; Mexico and the Other/HQ bucket consumed the difference. That concentration is the central fact of the equity story: any friction in Spanish activity flows straight through to group profit.

Management did not disclose a market share or ranking for Spain, and we have not located verified DGOJ share data for the quarter, so position versus bet365, Betano and the domestic leaders is n/a here. Nor is a sports net margin, structural margin or promo-as-%-of-handle disclosed at segment level; the only product colour is the group mix of 67% casino / 33% sports. The absence of handle disclosure means we cannot separate luck from volume in the Spanish sportsbook; the modest 7% spend-per-active growth implies no outsized margin tailwind.

The regulatory calendar is where the risk sits. New customer-identification and deposit requirements, including nominative payment methods, came into force for new customers at the end of October 2026 and will extend to existing customers in April 2027; joint deposit limits across all licensed operators follow in March 2027. Sher was candid that the new rules — which he framed as AML-driven rather than gambling-policy-driven — have already slowed the pace of acquisition, and that the fix is technological, with the company expecting to return to its prior acquisition cadence over the next few months. On the deposit limits, his argument is that they are default settings that players can raise through a verification process, that all operators face the same rules, and that incumbents with VIP relationships and the technology to manage the process are relatively advantaged; Arildsson added that the company will contact VIP customers directly ahead of the change. Our read: this is plausible but untested, and the Q4 single-digit guide explicitly bakes in 'transition effects' from Spain. The 2027 acquisition budget for Spain is said to be unchanged.

segments.name: Mexico
segments.headline: +39% Gaming Win is +26% in pesos, driven entirely by a 43% rise in spend per active while actives fell 3%; the 50% gaming-tax regime and marketing timing took Adj. EBITDA down to €1.7m.
narrative: Mexico remains the largest market at 55% of group Gaming Win. Revenue rose 37% to €32.9m (~$37.8m) and Gaming Win 39% to €37.2m (~$42.8m), with the gap between the two (€4.3m) reflecting the VAT and levy deductions taken before IFRS revenue; the revenue-to-Gaming-Win conversion slipped to 88% from 90%, consistent with a heavier tax wedge. Management was unusually direct that currency did much of the work: at constant currency Mexico grew 26%, so roughly 13 percentage points of the headline came from a stronger peso, and Arildsson noted the peso has 'given back most of its gains' against the euro since quarter-end. Sequentially Gaming Win rose 3% on Q2-26's €36.1m (~$41.5m), and nine-month Gaming Win is €107.8m (~$124.0m), +25%.

The composition of growth is the part a sceptic should dwell on. Average monthly actives declined 3% year-on-year to 85.6k (and 3% sequentially from 88.2k), while monthly spend per active rose 43% to roughly €145 (~$167). Management frames this as the payoff from deliberately improving customer quality, and it has been consistent on that theme for several quarters. The alternative reading is that a smaller, higher-spending cohort is both more profitable and more fragile, and that the World Cup tail in July and sports-margin luck — neither handle nor net sports margin is disclosed — may have inflated the per-head figure. Nine-month actives are still +6% to 90.7k, so the base has not shrunk over the year, but the sequential trend is down.

Profit did not follow revenue. Mexico Adj. EBITDA was €1.7m (~$2.0m) versus €2.0m (~$2.3m) a year ago, a 5.2% margin on revenue against 8.3%. Two things sit behind that: gaming taxes, which at group level rose 55% to €13.6m (~$15.6m) — far ahead of the 30% Gaming Win growth — in line with the Mexican 2026 fiscal package lifting the online gaming levy to 50% from 30% (per CasinoBeats; not verified in the filing); and marketing, which at group level rose 37% to €25.2m (~$29.0m), with Arildsson citing Mexican seasonality, the timing of certain provisions and expenses, and the translation effect of local-currency marketing into more euros, which he sized at 'a couple of million'. The consequence is that Mexico — 55% of Gaming Win — contributes roughly 40% of segment-level Adj. EBITDA before HQ costs, and that margin will not recover simply by lapping the tax step-up until early 2027.

The strategic push is brand. On 10 September Codere Online became Official Betting Partner of the NFL in Mexico under a multi-year agreement that includes sponsorship of the NFL Mexico City Game on 22 November 2026 and of Super Bowl LXI in February 2027, plus hospitality, VIP experiences and activations across multiple Mexican cities. That lands in Q4 marketing, with full-year marketing guided to the high-€90s (~$113-115m) against €86m (~$99m) in FY25. Market share and ranking in Mexico are not disclosed and we have no verified third-party figure; the company describes itself as a premium brand in a market where competition is 'intense'. Our judgement is that Mexico is the growth option but not yet the profit story, and that the Q4 setup — no FX help, a strong Q4-25 comp, NFL activation costs and a 50% levy — is the reason management refused to raise the EBITDA range despite a 45% Q3 beat on that line.

segments.name: Other markets (Colombia, Panama, City of Buenos Aires)
segments.headline: +86% Gaming Win on an easy Colombian tax comp; 8% of group, loss-making with HQ, and a possible 2027 Colombian deposit tax already has management talking about pulling investment.
narrative: The Other segment — Colombia, Panama and the City of Buenos Aires — generated Gaming Win of €5.2m (~$6.0m), up 86% year-on-year, and IFRS revenue of €4.9m (~$5.6m) against €1.6m (~$1.8m) a year ago, a comparison the company itself labels not meaningful. The lion's share of the improvement is Colombia lapping the 19% tax on customer deposits that applied through 2025 and depressed both activity and recognised revenue; Arildsson also singled out Panama as a consistent strong performer over 'many quarters'. Actives rose 37% to 28.4k and derived monthly spend per active rose roughly 35% to ~€61 (~$70), still less than half the Spanish or Mexican level. Sequentially the segment slipped 9% from Q2-26's €5.7m (~$6.6m), and nine-month Gaming Win is €15.3m (~$17.6m), +39%, on revenue of €14.3m (~$16.4m), +52%.

Profitability is not disclosed for the segment on its own. Backing Spain (€7.2m) and Mexico (€1.7m) out of group Adj. EBITDA (€4.2m) leaves roughly -€4.7m (~-$5.4m) for Other plus unallocated personnel and headquarter costs, versus about -€4.9m a year earlier — a marginal improvement that is consistent with Colombia moving toward break-even but gives no evidence of operating leverage in the central cost base. Argentina continues to be reported under IAS 29 hyperinflation accounting, with the monetary effect pushed through the interest line and reversed in 'Other adjustments', which is why segment and group EBITDA bridges should be read with care.

On outlook, the one new item was Colombia: management flagged that a deposit tax could return in 2027 and that, if it does, the company would reduce investment in the market rather than fight through it, as it effectively did in 2025. No formal market-share data is disclosed for any of the three jurisdictions, and no sports margin or promotional intensity is given. Our view is that this segment is optionality rather than thesis — it is too small to move group numbers and its growth rate is a function of tax policy more than of execution.

forecast.intro: Guidance was reiterated, not changed: FY26 Gaming Win €255-265m (~$293-305m) and Adj. EBITDA €20-25m (~$23-29m), both set on 30 Jul 2026 when they were raised from €235-245m and €15-20m. The reason it was not raised again after a +45% Adj. EBITDA quarter is Mexico and Spain in combination: Mexico loses the peso tailwind (~13pp of its Q3 growth) and carries the 50% gaming levy plus NFL activation spend into Q4, while Spain is absorbing AML-driven acquisition friction from end-October. Management translated that into 'single-digit' Q4 Gaming Win growth against a strong Q4-25 comp of €60.7m (~$69.8m). Arithmetically the range implies Q4-26 Gaming Win of €54-64m (~$62-74m; -11% to +5% YoY) and Q4-26 Adj. EBITDA of €3.9-8.9m (~$4.5-10.2m) versus €6.7m (~$7.7m) in Q4-25 (derived from FY25 €13.8m less 9M-25 €7.1m). The 'upper part' language on Gaming Win implies ~€62-64m for Q4, i.e. +2-5%.

forecast.view: **Q4-26 (our estimate):** Gaming Win ~€62-63m (~$71-72m), +2-4% YoY, with Spain roughly flat-to-slightly-down on AML friction and Mexico +5-8% in euros as the peso reversal offsets underlying mid-teens local-currency growth. Adj. EBITDA ~€4.5-6.0m (~$5-7m) — below Q4-25's €6.7m — on a Q4 marketing bill of roughly €25-27m (~€100m FY less ~€73-75m 9M, itself an estimate since 9M marketing was not disclosed) and a full quarter of the Mexican levy. That lands FY26 Gaming Win at ~€263m (~$302m, top of range) and **FY26 Adj. EBITDA at ~€20.5-22m (~$24-25m), low-to-mid range** — i.e. the Gaming Win guide is conservative, the EBITDA guide is not. **FY27:** management's framing (marketing flat in absolute terms, falling as % of Gaming Win) implies mid-teens Gaming Win growth and an Adj. EBITDA margin on Gaming Win moving from ~8% toward 10-11%, but only if Spain's March/April 2027 deposit-limit and ID extensions prove as benign as claimed and Colombia does not reinstate a deposit tax. We would haircut Mexican local-currency growth to low-teens post-World Cup and watch whether actives stabilise; a cohort that is 3% smaller spending 43% more is not a base to extrapolate. **Leverage:** stays net cash; cash should end FY26 around €68-70m (~$78-80m) absent M&A, with the LTIP cash-tax element and warrant volatility the only non-operating drains. **Swing factors:** MXN/EUR, Spanish FTD recovery pace, sports margin in a non-tournament Q4, and the parent's break-up process — a sale of Codere Online as a standalone would change the free float, the shareholder agreement and potentially the platform/brand licensing arrangements with Codere Group.
watch: Q4-26 Gaming Win vs the €60.7m (~$69.8m) comp — whether 'single-digit' lands positive (upper-range) or the range is used to absorb Spain friction.
Spanish FTD run-rate through Nov-Jan after the end-October ID/nominative-payment rules, and the March 2027 cross-operator deposit-limit go-live.
MXN/EUR: ~13pp of Mexico's Q3 growth was FX; CFO says most of it has already reversed since 30 Sep.
Mexico Adj. EBITDA margin under the 50% gaming levy and NFL activation; whether Mexican actives stabilise after two sequential declines.
FY26 marketing landing (~€100m / ~$115m guided) and the FY27 budget — does marketing finally grow slower than Gaming Win?
LTIP expense (€7.6m 9M) and the cash-tax element; warrant fair-value swings in reported net income; EPS disclosure.
Codere Group break-up sale (Expansión, 2 Nov 2026): a standalone sale of Codere Online would be a change-of-control event for a controlled company.
Colombia 2027 deposit-tax decision and any associated pull-back in investment; Argentina IAS 29 effects.
